name: Mitsubishi
overview: From manufacturing over 1.1 million cars at Tonsley Park, South Australia to dominating outback tracks with the Pajero and Triton, Mitsubishi is embedded in Australia's automotive fabric.
australian_history:
Mitsubishi's connection with Australia began in the 1960s through Chrysler Australia, which sold the Colt 1000 and, in 1971, introduced the Galant. In 1977, Chrysler Australia launched the Chrysler Sigma (based on the Japanese Galant), assembled at Chrysler's Tonsley Park plant in Adelaide, South Australia. The Sigma became an instant national sensation, dominating the 4-cylinder market.

In 1980, Mitsubishi Motors Corporation acquired Chrysler Australia, establishing Mitsubishi Motors Australia Limited (MMAL). MMAL invested heavily in South Australia, operating vehicle assembly at Tonsley Park and an engine casting foundry at Lonsdale. In 1985, MMAL launched the groundbreaking TM Magna. Engineered specifically for Australian family motoring, MMAL took the Japanese Galant and widened the body by 66mm to create a spacious mid-to-large car perfectly suited to Australian wide-open spaces. Powered by the locally made 2.6L Astron II engine, the Magna won the 1985 Wheels Car of the Year.

In 1991, MMAL launched the second-generation TR Magna and luxury KR Verada, introducing a 3.0L V6. The Australian-developed Magna wagon and sedan were exported in huge numbers to the United States (as the Mitsubishi Diamante), Japan, and the UK, demonstrating world-class Australian manufacturing capability. In 1996, the third-generation TE Magna won Wheels Car of the Year again. In 2002, MMAL created the Magna Ralliart (180kW hand-built 3.5L V6) and the world-first Magna All-Wheel Drive (AWD) utilizing the QuadTec system. In 2005, the Magna was replaced by the 380 sedan (DB series) following a $600M plant overhaul. However, shifting consumer demand away from large local sedans led MMAL to close Tonsley Park on March 27, 2008.

Following the end of domestic manufacturing, Mitsubishi successfully pivoted to a 100% imported range focused on SUVs and utes. The Pajero established legendary 4WD status across four generations (1983-2021). The Triton ute became one of Australia's top three light commercial vehicles. In 2014, the Outlander PHEV pioneered affordable plug-in hybrid technology in Australia, remaining the nation's best-selling PHEV SUV.

models.name: Magna
models.overview: The Mitsubishi Magna was an Australian manufacturing triumph, designed specifically for Australian conditions by widening the Japanese Galant by 66mm. Produced at Tonsley Park in Adelaide, it won two Wheels Car of the Year awards (1985, 1996) and culminated in the 180kW Magna Ralliart and revolutionary Magna AWD.

The Mitsubishi 380 was the final passenger car designed, engineered, and manufactured by Mitsubishi Motors Australia at its Tonsley Park plant in Adelaide. Backed by a $600-million investment and over 2.4 million kilometres of Australian testing, the 380 was powered by a punchy 3.8-litre 6G75 V6 with 175kW and 343Nm, praised by critics for its exceptionally stiff body structure and European-grade chassis dynamics.

380.overview: The Mitsubishi 380 was the final passenger car designed, engineered, and manufactured by Mitsubishi Motors Australia at its Tonsley Park plant in Adelaide. Backed by a $600-million investment and over 2.4 million kilometres of Australian testing, the 380 was powered by a punchy 3.8-litre 6G75 V6 with 175kW and 343Nm, praised by critics for its exceptionally stiff body structure and European-grade chassis dynamics.
380.australian_market_notes: Launched in October 2005 to replace the Magna and Verada, the 380 went toe-to-toe with the Holden Commodore and Ford Falcon. While acclaimed by Wheels and Motor for chassis rigidity and refined ride quality, intense fleet competition and soaring fuel prices hampered sales volumes. Series II and III introduced revised equipment and competitive pricing. The final Mitsubishi 380 rolled off the Tonsley Park production line on 27 March 2008, bringing to an end 43 years of vehicle assembly at the Adelaide factory.

lancer-evolution.name: Lancer Evolution & Ralliart
lancer-evolution.overview: The Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution and Ralliart models represent one of the greatest chapters in modern Australian performance car folklore. Born directly from World Rally Championship battles where Tommi Mäkinen claimed four consecutive WRC drivers' titles, the Evo delivered staggering turbocharged all-wheel-drive grip, Active Yaw Control (AYC), and giant-killing cross-country pace.
lancer-evolution.australian_market_notes: Australian enthusiasts first tasted this formula with the 1992-1996 Lancer GSR 4WD (CC). In 2001, Team Mitsubishi Ralliart officially imported 100 numbered examples of the iconic Evo 6.5 Tommi Mäkinen Edition (TME). From the Evo VIII in 2004, Mitsubishi Australia officially retailed Evolution models through selected Ralliart dealerships. The story culminated in the high-tech aluminium 4B11T-powered Evo X and the 226kW Final Edition in 2015.

starion-cordia.name: Starion & Cordia Turbo
starion-cordia.overview: The Mitsubishi Starion Turbo and Cordia GSR Turbo were the trailblazers of Japanese factory turbocharging in 1980s Australia. From the front-wheel drive Cordia GSR with its mind-bending 'Super Shift' 4x2 twin-stick dual-range transmission to the widebody, rear-wheel drive Starion Turbo that battled Australian Touring Cars in Group E and Group A, these coupes created Australia's turbo street-racing legend.
starion-cordia.australian_market_notes: Released in 1982 (Starion) and 1983 (Cordia), Mitsubishi brought boost to Australian showrooms years before it became mainstream. The lightweight Cordia GSR Turbo with digital instrumentation became a 1980s street-racer folklore hero, while the Starion was famously campaigned by rally ace Colin Bond in the Australian Production Car Championship and Bathurst 1000 with factory Ralliart backing.

triton.name: Triton
triton.overview: The Mitsubishi Triton has been one of Australia's favourite dual-cab utes for over four decades, offering tough ladder-chassis capability, advanced Super Select II 4WD, and exceptional value for trades and families.
triton.australian_market_notes: First sold as the L200 in 1979, the Triton badge was established in 1986. The fourth-generation ML introduced the distinctive curved 'J-line' cabin, while the MQ and MR brought the lightweight 2.4L 4N15 MIVEC aluminium turbo-diesel and full-time 4WD on sealed surfaces via Super Select II. In 2024, the all-new MV Triton arrived with bi-turbo diesel power and 3500kg towing.

pajero.name: Pajero
pajero.overview: With 12 victories in the grueling Dakar Rally, the Mitsubishi Pajero is one of the world's most successful four-wheel drives. In Australia, it defined the family 4WD wagon for nearly four decades across four generations.
pajero.australian_market_notes: First imported in 1983, the Pajero transformed four-wheel driving from farm machinery to comfortable family transport. The NH generation introduced Super Select 4WD, allowing full-time AWD on dry bitumen and locking 4WD on dirt. The NM series brought a revolutionary monocoque chassis with independent suspension. After 38 years and over 175,000 sales in Australia, production concluded in 2021 with the Pajero Final Edition.
